        Pursuant to section 203(a)(1) of the Federal Power Act, as amended (“FPA”), 1 and Part 33

of the regulations of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “Commission”), 2

Twin Ridges LLC (“Twin Ridges”) and Laurel Run Interconnection LLC (“Laurel Run” and,

together with Twin Ridges, the “Applicants”) hereby submit this application (“Application”)

requesting authorization for the disposition of jurisdictional facilities resulting from the potential

transfer of certain Interconnection Customer’s Interconnection Facilities (“ICIF”) from Twin

Ridges to Laurel Run (the “Transaction”). The Applicants are each indirect wholly-owned

subsidiaries of Exus US Holdings, LP (“Exus US Holdings”). Following consummation of the

Transaction, Laurel Run will directly own 100 percent of the ICIF.

    VI.       DESCRIPTION OF THE TRANSACTION

         Pursuant to the Transaction, Laurel Run will directly acquire Twin Ridges’ ICIF (and any

associated books and records). Following the consummation of the Transaction, Twin Ridges and

Sugar Maple (upon completion of its generating facility) will each use a pro rata portion of the

ICIF (in proportion to their ownership interests in Laurel Run) to deliver the electrical output of

their facilities to the PJM-administered grid pursuant to a Shared Facilities Agreement that will be

filed with the Commission.

         The material terms of the Transaction are summarized in the Term Sheet included as

confidential Exhibit I to this Application. Applicants request confidential treatment of the Term

Sheet because it contains sensitive commercial and financial information that is not publicly

available.

         As described below, the Transaction will have no adverse effect on competition, rates, or

regulation, and does not raise any cross-subsidization issues. Further, the Transaction will not

affect the ultimate upstream ownership of the affected jurisdictional facilities and will not result

in any new affiliations, any increase in generating capacity, or any new vertical inputs.

Accordingly, Applicants request that the Commission issue an order approving the Transaction as

described herein.



   VI.       REQUEST FOR FPA SECTION 203 APPROVAL

         Applicants seek Commission authorization for the Transaction under FPA section

203(a)(1) because Twin Ridges is a public utility that would be disposing part of its jurisdictional

facilities with a value (i.e., undepreciated or the original book cost) in excess of $10 million.


                                                 12
          Section 203(a)(4) of the FPA provides that the Commission will authorize jurisdictional

transactions that are “consistent with the public interest.” As explained in the Merger Policy

Statement, 30 Order No. 642, 31 and Order No. 669, 32 the Commission examines three factors in

determining whether a proposed transaction is consistent with the public interest: (i) its effect on

competition; (ii) its effect on rates; and (iii) its effect on regulation. Importantly, the Commission

has determined that for a transaction to be found “consistent with the public interest,” an applicant

need not show that a transaction inures to the benefit of the public interest, but rather that the

transaction does not harm the public interest. 33 In addition, FPA section 203(a)(4) requires a

showing that a proposed transaction will not result in cross-subsidization of a non-utility associate

company or pledge or encumbrance of utility assets for the benefit of an associate company. 34

         Applicants respectfully submit that the Commission should conclude, based on the

information contained in this Application, that the Transaction is consistent with the public interest

because it will not have an adverse effect on competition, rates, or regulation and will not result in

the cross-subsidization of a non-utility associate company or the pledge or encumbrance of utility

assets for the benefit of an associate company. Further, the Transaction will not affect the ultimate

        A.      The Transaction Will Have No Adverse Effect on Competition

        The Transaction will have no adverse effect on competition. The Transaction does not

involve any generation facilities and therefore does not raise any horizontal market power

concerns. Rather, the Transaction is limited to changes in the ownership of limited and discrete

interconnection equipment that constitutes ICIF. The Commission has indicated that the

disposition of transmission assets generally does not raise competitive concerns and has exempted

applicants from providing the competitive screens otherwise required by sections 33.3 and 33.4 of

the Commission’s regulations. 35 Further, in Order No. 669, the Commission stated, “[i]t also has

been our experience that anticompetitive effects are unlikely to arise with regard to . . . transactions

that only involve the disposition of transmission facilities.” 36

        Moreover, the Transaction is comprised of affiliate transactions and will not result in any

new affiliation or combination of electric generation facilities, transmission facilities, or inputs to

generation. The limited and discrete interconnection and transmission facilities involved in the

Transaction are ICIF and qualify for the blanket waiver from the Commission’s OATT

requirements pursuant to section 35.28(d)(2) of the Commission’s regulations, which mitigates

any vertical market power concerns. The Transaction does not involve any inputs to electricity

pledge, or encumbrance will be consistent with the public interest. 38 The Commission has stated

that the concern over cross-subsidization is principally a concern over the effect of a proposed

transaction on captive ratepayers. 39
